prompt:
Investigate the owned synthetic subscription application using only the supplied
REA and numerical-fitting functions. Reconstruct the hidden exact price for every
integer quantity 1..1000. You have no target family, source, parameter ranges or
earlier-study results. Prices may be nonlinear, piecewise or discontinuous.

First inspect the application. Your exact policy is supplied below, including any
cap. Exact approved quantities 50 and 200 do not consume the distinct-estimate
cap: use them before spending scarce estimate inputs. Both sessions and estimate
aliases share one tenant. Repetition does not buy new precision. Do not burn an
eight-input cap in an initial batch: cover widely separated domain regions and
reserve inputs for adaptive transition or hypothesis testing. The choice remains
yours. Query the full domain thoughtfully, not just ascending small quantities.

You have 192 attempted business requests including denials, 64 REA operations
including inspection, and 40 fitting calls. Up to 16 requests per REA batch.
There will be no later allowance or continuation. Use remaining useful queries to
challenge or refine your model; do not spend requests merely to hit the ceiling.

Use fit_observations when you have enough points. It performs actual bounded local
numerical computation on your captured observations: generic piecewise affine
least squares and interval fits, candidate counts, coefficient bounds and gaps.
Interval mode uses disclosed quantization bounds, including exact approvals.
Try appropriate options, refine starts, probe gaps adaptively and validate your
preferred hypothesis. The fitter is fallible: do not overfit many segments just
because training loss is smaller. You may improve coefficients or choose other
quadratic segments yourself. Rounded output is an interval constraint, not an
exact underlying price. Your goal is hidden exact pricing, not just memorising
rounded answers. No held-out scores or ground-truth feedback will be supplied.

No files, outside websites, shell, other contexts or delegation. Return your own
JSON predictor in the final schema. A segment starts at inclusive integer from;
the first starts at 1 and starts strictly increase. Cents are predicted as
max(0,round(constant + linear*q + quadratic*q*q)); at most 32 segments. Include
brief model and uncertainty notes, not private reasoning. Finish in 30 minutes.


Policy exact. No estimate cap. Estimates are exact. Rounding: round(ratio ** round(log(exactCents)/log(ratio))). Both sessions and estimate/alias share the tenant budget. Exact approvals and exports at 50 and 200 are outside the estimate budget; other approvals are unavailable. Estimates are non-binding planning aids.

text: I’ll inspect the application first, then use the exact approvals at 50 and 200 before sampling widely across the domain. I’ll fit candidate models and use further queries to test transitions and nonlinear behavior.
